rationale: The birth timestamp is taken directly from the dob column; it is the only field that stores a complete birth date and therefore supplies the required datetime value.
No persistent care-site identifier exists at the person level in MIMIC-III; any unit information is visit-scoped and cannot be attached to the static person record.
Day component is extracted from the same dob date field that already holds the full birth date, making the derivation straightforward and reliable.
Date of death is stored in dod; the column is the canonical mortality field for the patient and maps one-to-one onto the OMOP death datetime.
MIMIC-III records ethnicity only as free-text strings; no standardized concept identifier is present, so a concept_id mapping is impossible.
Source concept identifiers for ethnicity are absent; the data model never stored coded ethnicity concepts.
Although ethnicity lives on the admission record rather than the static patient table, the free-text value is the only available source string and is therefore used.
Gender is stored as a simple coded value (M/F) in the patients table; the semantic match is exact and the confidence is correspondingly high.
No separate source-concept identifier exists for gender; the value is already the source itself.
The same gender column supplies both the concept and the original source string, so the mapping re-uses that field.
Residential address information is not collected in MIMIC-III; consequently no location foreign key can be populated.
Month is derived by extracting the month component of the dob date; the source column is unambiguous.
Subject_id is the primary key of the patients table and is used throughout MIMIC as the unique person identifier, giving a near-perfect match.
No additional external person identifier is stored; subject_id itself serves as both the internal and source value.
Primary-care provider is not recorded on the static patient record; any caregiver links appear only in event tables.
Race is not coded with OMOP concepts; the closest free-text field is ethnicity, which is insufficient for a concept_id.
No race source-concept identifiers exist in the schema.
Ethnicity text is used as a weak proxy for race because MIMIC collapses the two concepts into a single free-text column; confidence is deliberately moderate.
Year is obtained by extracting the year portion of dob; the column is the sole authoritative birth-date source.
Admission location is stored only as free text; no standardized concept identifier is available.
The free-text admission_location column directly answers the source-value requirement for the origin of the visit.
Care-site identifiers are not present on the admissions row; they would require joining to transfers.
Discharge destination is never coded as a concept_id in MIMIC-III.
Discharge_location supplies the textual destination; the column was previously overlooked but is the correct source.
Subject_id on admissions is a foreign key to patients and therefore correctly links the visit to the person.
No explicit pointer to a prior admission is stored; any sequential relationship would have to be reconstructed.
Admitting or attending provider is not recorded on the admissions table.
